dedupe_keys.name: inema high resolution inventory of atmospheric emissions from anthrophogenic sectors in chile

description: Universidad de Chile and Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María publish INEMA, a gridded inventory of Chilean anthropogenic emissions. It separates transport, industrial, energy, mining and residential activities, with pollutant totals distributed to a 0.01 degree latitude-longitude grid. The repository describes carbon dioxide and several air pollutants, with additional species for selected source sectors. TAR archives contain NetCDF grids expressed in gigagrams per year. Access is open and free under CC-BY-4.0. The description states 2015–2020, but the exposed file inventory in this version lists sector archives for 2015–2017; users should resolve this coverage discrepancy before time comparisons. Emissions are estimated from activity data and emission factors, not direct measurements at every grid cell. These inputs could compare environmental consequences of transport or energy scenarios, or supply source terms for an atmospheric model around infrastructure. They complement asset and traffic inventories with estimated emissions; they do not represent plant connectivity or operational capacity.
